plain: Speaking against someone to damage his good name.

webster.text: The act of taking something from the reputation or worth of another, with the view to lessen him in estimation; censure; a lessening of worth; the act of depreciating another, from envy or malice.

example.quote: Let him convince me by reasoning, but not fall on detraction or declamation.
example.cite: Jonathan Elliot, ed., The Debates in the Several State Conventions on the Adoption of the Federal Constitution, vol. 4, North Carolina Convention, Mr. J. TAYLOR, July 25, 1788 (2d ed. 1836)
